The number retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

3.1.4.2 As far as possible the bag cargo for palletization should be in gusseted walled bags and so packed to give a flat all round shape and the same to be vacuum packed to avoid air movement and resultant slacking of the unit pallet. 3.1.4.3 2-way or 4-way pallets can be used for these packages, It will be preferable to select 2-way pallects with 4 No. stringer ( beam ) for maximum dimension pallets and maximum unit load. 5.1 The packages ( wooden or plywood cases/cartoon/sacks, etc ) shall be stacked on the deck-board of the pallets for uniformity in interlocking svstem by keeping the surface flat ( where possi~ble ). The overall height of the pallets shall not exceed I 100 mm.

5.2 At the time of stacking the packages on the deck-board, it should be carefully observed that no packages should come out from the dimension of the pallets to prevent damage and loss of space. If the packages are bigger than the dimension of pallets ( where the maximum dimension of pallets are used ), the container space will be lost. 6 STRAPPING/WRAPPING all the wooden cases/plywood/barrel/ drum cargoes, iron strap shall be of 16 to 22 mm width and O-45 to 0.55 mm thickness correspond to Grade 2 of IS 5872 : 1973. The strap shall be fastened as tightly as possible. 6.2 For all the cargoes which can be damaged by steel strap like sacks, paper, hessian or polythene cartons/corrugated paper board Dr fiberboard box and trust packages, polypropylene strap shall be of 16 to 22 mm width. The strap shall be tightened as tightly as possible. 6.3 Number of straps ~to be used and method of their tightening for different types of load pack-

6.1 For

6.3.1 For all the containerization palletized load cargo, all the 4-way pallets, the vertical straps on 1 000 mm side ( i.e. width side ) of the pallets should go under the bottom layer of the cargo packages but over the deck-board of the pallets. This is to prevent the fork-lift prongs getting entangled with the strap durmg handling. 6.4

Shrink Wrapping

It is suitable for light weight and homogeneous load cargo, preferable for cardboard cartoon/ corrugated box/ply-wood case or chest and flat top and bottom with vacuum filled sacks. Low density pnlythene with appropriate gauge should be used. Minimum four corner should be shrink properly.

Standard Mark

Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by-the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations

The use of the Standard

Bnreay of Indian Standards

.

BIS Is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standa& Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations; Enquiries relating to copyright be addresred to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest -amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and Standards Monthly Additions'. Comments on thin Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving the following reference1 Dot : No. HMD 11 ( 0018 )
